pistons.headline: The Pistons go from owning to getting owned in the paint
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Jalen Duren #0 of the Detroit Pistons looks on from the bench during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

During a tumultuous playoff run and a prolonged offseason contract negotiation, Detroit Pistons fans were ready to say goodbye to Jalen Duren. Well, Duren has been out for six of eight games, and it turns out that Duren is the most indispensable member of the Pistons aside from Cade Cunningham.

A hamstring strain has knocked Duren out for six straight and counting, and boy, do you feel that every moment of every Pistons game.

Pundits and fans alike had easy diagnoses for what ailed the 60-win team during a disappointing second-round exit last season. Detroit needed a second scorer and much more perimeter shooting to succeed in the postseason. Its second-best player, the All-NBA big man Duren, couldn’t effectively operate in a congested, constipated offense when opponents had so much extra time to prepare their defense. That had a trickle-down effect on Cade Cunningham and on offensively limited players the Pistons relied on, like Ausar Thompson, Javonte Green, and Ron Holland.

This offseason, the Pistons seemingly tried and failed to add their second scorer (a planned run at Austin Reaves fizzled, and trade interest in players such as Kyrie Irving and Kevin Durant went nowhere). But they certainly addressed the team’s lack of perimeter punch. Detroit added guys such as Isaiah Joe, John Collins, and Taurean Prince. They re-signed midseason acquisition Kevin Huerter. They reformulated their offensive game plan to create more movement, space, and offensive responsibility among their non-Cade players. So far this season, the perimeter offense has hummed. Detroit is a top-10 team in 3-point shooting and almost middle of the pack in attempts despite Isaiah Joe missing most of the season to injury.

Detroit is 6-2, losing to the New York Knicks and on Wednesday night to the East-leading Philadelphia 76ers. Calls after both games from fans and casual watchers immediately turn to the team’s lack of that second star as the biggest issue. While that still might be a deal-breaker in the players, I would argue that the actual biggest issue in the season’s first eight games is Detroit’s collapse in its former ability to absolutely own the paint.

In other words, it’s not the lack of a Kyrie or a Durant or a Devin Booker. It’s the lack of Duren.

Last season, Detroit led the NBA in points in the paint, mostly behind Duren’s elite rim gravity and chemistry with Cade Cunningham and Detroit’s other ball handlers. Last season, the Pistons led the NBA with 57.9 points in the paint and were fourth in opponents’ paint scoring. They had a scoring differential inside of 14.2 points per game.  This season, Detroit ranks just 22nd in the paint at 44.8, down 13.1 points per game.

Rim gravity, it turns out, is just as important as perimeter shooting in creating the space needed to run a successful offense.

Paul Reed is a dynamic scorer inside, and he has some pop to his game. But he isn’t a rim runner like Duren. You give it to him on the block, and you let him work his magic. John Collins is opportunistic in transition, but those opportunities are dried up when he is the only big on the floor applying rim pressure, usually trying to duck in from the corners.

Ausar has the ball in his hands more, and it is working to create opportunities from others on the perimeter, but it is taking away a lot of those dunker-spot opportunities and back cuts that Thompson feasted on last season.

The lack of inside pressure is manifesting in other ways. Detroit has gone from a top-5 team in second-chance points to 22nd. They are 28th in offensive rebounding. Last season, they were third.

This team needs Jalen Duren back ASAP. And I think fans need to start reckoning with how crucial he is for this team to succeed.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs 76ers final score: Detroit falls short in East battle
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons drives around Vj Edgecombe #77 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons (6-2) fall short in the battle between the top teams in the Eastern Conference. The Philadelphia 76ers (8-1) outlasted Detroit 112-106. Philly got up by as many as 18 points, but Detroit never truly went away. The 76ers’ stardom showed its head tonight.

After holding Jaylen Brown to 16 points in the first meeting of the season, he surpassed that in the first half this time around. Brown poured in 30 points for the game while converting on 11 of his 19 shots. He rained in spot-up 3s, as it was tough to stick with him with the way Philly forced Detroit into scramble mode throughout the ballgame. Brown had a clutch block on Cade, and his presence was felt on both sides of the ball.

This is not 2023 Joel Embiid, but he’s still a force. Embiid still draws double teams and can get any big in foul trouble. He and Tolu Smith got into a dust-up that injected some life into Detroit, but Philly found a way to withstand every Detroit storm.

Duncan Robinson went on a few personal runs that seemed to turn the tide in Detroit’s favor. The sharpshooter went for 27 points and buried an unconscious seven triples. Robinson’s ability to look past the hands in his face to shoot the rock will pay dividends all season. It didn’t work out tonight, but Robinson is off to a different type of start as a sniper.

Cade Cunningham tried to put on his cape and emptied the clip. He couldn’t find it from deep but got good looks. He went for 26 points, 11 assists, and seven boards. He got to the charity stripe and nailed every attempt (7-7). Cade had another LeBron-like chasedown block — this time in LeBron’s presence.

At this point, those are truly Cade-like chasedowns, and Brown’s missed layup here shows Cade’s reputation as a chasedown artist is evident.

Jaylen Brown misses the wide open layup. 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMyfS41RJG
— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) November 5, 2026

VJ Edgecombe had a fast break sequence where he u-turned it because Cade was on the hunt again. Special defender.

Ausar Thompson’s special stuff came on the boards as he snagged 17 rebounds tonight. From the opening possession, he was pogo-sticking down low to help Paul Reed and John Collins in the paint. AT chipped in 11 points, and his shot from the line continues to look better. He was 3-for-4 tonight; you’ll take the small improvements wherever you can.

John Collins had his best offensive game in a few games. He was getting behind the defense, throwing down head-top slams. His ability to be a paint finisher and hit threes is why he’s here. He only shot one 3 tonight. The Pistons need more.

Collins should look better when Duren comes back, in theory. Duren has rim-gravity that forces defenses to account for one of the best finishers in basketball. This was the first game where I thought Detroit missed Duren badly. From a talent perspective, Detroit was outgunned tonight.

LeBron James controlled the tempo in spurts of the game. He was playing like that OG at the Y who’s keeping up with the youngins on pure know-how. LeBron draws two to the ball, Embiid does, Brown does, and Tyrese Maxey does. There’s a lot of star power over there, and this is a team Detroit could see in the long run.

The Pistons did not have their sharpest defensive night, and Philly still only cracked 112. It was just one of the games. Detroit shifts their focus to another superstar in Luka Dončić. He and the Los Angeles Lakers travel to Detroit on Sunday as the Pistons take on their first Western Conference team of the season.

The Detroit Pistons are looking to keep the good times rolling against the Philadelphia 76ers. Detroit and Philly are the two best teams in the East, and the Pistons have already notched one win against the Sixers this season. In fact, the 106-93 win in October was Detroit’s sixth consecutive victory against Philly. Tonight, they go for lucky No. 7. That loss against the Pistons also happens to be Philadelphia’s lone blemish on the season. In that matchup, the Pistons were without the services of Jalen Duren. It worked out because they were able to rely on the all-around goodness of Paul Reed. It also didn’t hurt that Joel Embiid missed that first matchup to rest.

Tonight, the Pistons will have no such luck. They are still missing All-Star big man Duren, and tonight the Sixers will employ the services of their former MVP in Embiid. While Detroit has been playing amazing basketball, they have been vulnerable down low, and Embiid will be the best interior big man they’ve faced since they lost Duren to a hamstring injury.

One benefit in Detroit’s favor is that this is a nationally televised game on ESPN, and it seems like Cade Cunningham loves to come up big when the lights are brightest for national television. Cunningham is also coming off of perhaps his most dominant performance of the season, scoring 33 points in just 26 minutes of action. If the game against the Hornets was close instead of a 30-point blowout late, if seems like Cunningham could have gone for 45 points.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs 76ers preview:  East’s top two teams square off on National TV
pistons.body:
If you are to believe preseason predictions, this game being a showdown between the East’s top two teams could come as a bit of a surprise.  Pistons fans knew this team would be good, but many talking heads predicted a falloff this season while everybody was on board with the 76ers being one of the best teams in the league.

It shouldn’t come as a surprise that the team that was 1st in the East last season is once again competing for the top seed in the East, but talking heads have to make their money somehow.  ESPN at least had the foresight to pickup this game and you get what should be a very fun early-season showdown between two teams that have only lost one game each.

The 76ers and Pistons have played once this season and the Pistons won, but it is tough to draw any conclusions since both teams were missing a couple of starters.

Game Vitals

Where:  Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, MI
When:  Wednesday, November 4 at 7 pm EST
Watch:  ESPN
Odds:  Detroit (-2.5)

Analysis

The Pistons will be without Jalen Duren and Isaiah Joe, who was already ruled out for this game last night.  The Pistons were missing Jalen Duren in the last matchup between these teams and also Ausar Thompson, who they will have back.  But, Isaiah Joe did suffer the hip injury that is still keeping him out during the 1st quarter of the last matchup, so the Pistons are trading one injured player for another.

With this being a National TV game and the 76ers getting a day of rest, I would suspect that everybody plays for them tonight.  In the last matchup, the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid or VJ Edgecombe, which really put their lack of depth to the test.

Joel Embiid’s size and ability on the glass could become a problem for the Pistons, who will continue to start the undersized Paul Reed and likely use John Collins to back him up.  Without Jalen Duren, rebounding was already going to be a problem, but the Pistons have been able to overcome it during his absence.

In the last matchup, the Pistons were able to contain Tyrese Maxey through 3 quarters before he started hitting shots in the 4th.  It was a bit of shocking development since the Pistons were without Ausar Thompson, but without some of the other stars for the 76ers, they could focus their defense more on stopping Maxey.  The 76ers have a lot of star power, but their biggest offensive threat is arguably Maxey, who can hit shots from anywhere on the court and can use his quickness with the ball to get to where he wants.  I would expect Ausar Thompson to draw the Tyrese Maxey matchup which will allow Cade Cunningham to guard Jaylen Brown since he has the size to keep up with him.

I am not really sure what the Pistons are going to do about the Joel Embiid matchup.  Paul Reed is outsized by him and also can have some issues with fouling and Joel Embiid has made a living off of bating fouls throughout his career.  Paul Reed is going to have to stay disciplined, as I don’t think the Pistons can afford to have heavy minutes of John Collins at center or Tolu Smith.  I have full confidence in the Pistons’ ability to matchup with the rest of the 76ers starting lineup, but the most concern I have is this matchup and it very well could swing the game.

If there is one certainty for the Pistons, it is that Cade Cunningham is difficult to slow down, especially with how he is playing now.  He is coming off a 33 points masterclass against the Charlotte Hornets on Monday in only 27 minutes where he absolutely took over the game and turned a single-digit lead into a 20-plus point blowout.  Cade Cunningham always starts off the season slow, but he seems to be hitting his stride now.  His 3-ball is consistently falling as he is shooting 37% from beyond the arc, which is a significant development for his offensive creation abilities and efficiency.

He is going to have to put together another masterclass if the Pistons want any hope to win this game.  During Jalen Duren’s absence, the Pistons have been able to win games through their high-level defense, but their offense has left a lot to be desired.  With Isaiah Joe out and Duncan Robinson going through a bit of a cold stretch, the Pistons shooting fell off a bit and they went four games in a row scoring 110 points or less.

However, everything seemed to get back on track on Monday against the Hornets, so hopefully that continues.

One player the Pistons are hoping gets back on track is John Collins.  He had his best game as a Piston in the last game against the 76ers and has proceeded to score single-digit points in every game since then.  With Jalen Duren out, he has had to play a lot more center than he was probably planning on playing, but he has also had difficulties finding a consistent offensive role.  Another big John Collins game would be a huge help in this matchup

The Joel Embiid matchup concerns me with the Pistons lack of frontcourt size, but if they can defend Tyrese Maxey like they did in the last matchup, they have a shot to takedown the 76ers and claim the top seed in the Eastern Conference.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (6-1):  Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Paul Reed

Philadelphia 76ers (7-1):  Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Joel Embiid

Question of the Day

Which of these teams will finish higher in the Eastern Conference at the end of the season?

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Hornets final score: Cade Cunningham powers second-half surge in blowout win
pistons.body:
CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 2: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 2, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons played great basketball throughout the night, but the Charlotte Hornets just kept hanging around. The Pistons were shooting better than 60% from the floor and 50% from three, and yet a Dennis Schroder layup made it a two-possession game with just under five minutes left in the second quarter. Then Cade Cunningham took over, then the Detroit Pistons took over, and suddenly a squeaker turned into a 124-91 Detroit win.

In that decisive 45-16 run, Cade Cunningham scored 14 points, and he did it in under three and a half minutes of game time. One of the league’s best players finally had his first superstar quarter of the season, scoring 17 points and notching three assists in total in that decisive third frame. He finished the night with 33 points, seven assists, and five steals. In those magical few minutes, he was everywhere in his bag. Patient mid-range pull-ups, slicing through the D for layups, catch-and-shoot threes. He went to the bench with 1:17 left in the third quarter, and you were left thinking he might hit 50 in the fourth. But he never needed to come back in the game again.

He saw the game was getting too close, and he decided to do something about it. He put the team on his back and said, “We’re playing too well to not blow these guys out.”

But the true blowout wouldn’t have happened without all the other contributions up and down the lineup. The Pistons really have something on offense this season, and while the range of ball handlers and actions can lead to some self-inflicted wounds, it is designed to open up this offense and let it breathe. And, boy, did they take a big gulping breath versus the Hornets.

The Pistons shot 57% from the floor and 48% from deep, and that was dragged down a bit as a consequence of some extended garbage time. The Pistons also kept their defense in top form. They forced 25 Charlotte turnovers, and that led to 27 fast-break points.

Detroit was led by Cade, but Duncan Robinson continues to be lights out this season. He shot 6-of-9 from deep on his way to 24 points. His stroke was immediate and effortless. He’s truly in the zone. Some of that shooting magic might be rubbing off on Kevin Huerter. The one-time bucket has struggled from deep for a few seasons now, including his short stint after a mid-season trade to Detroit last season. But he hit three threes tonight and is now shooting 38% from deep for the season. Even Ron Holland canned three threes tonight. Not to be overlooked is Ausar Thompson’s expanded role in the offense.

It’s not always perfect, but Thompson is getting more comfortable making decisions with the ball in his hands, and he’s understanding how to make defense pay by using his strength and burst to get something close to the basket. Thompson was 5-of-7 from the floor for 14 points, and he added six rebounds and four assists.

The Pistons had plenty of lopsided runs last season in their sprint to 60 wins. But those were driven by a defense that would suffocate you and an offense that could do just enough. Last year, the Pistons could go on a 27-2 run over the course of 17 minutes of game action. Tonight, they went on the same run in just over eight minutes.

Detroit’s defense remains the best in the league. Its offense is starting to catch up. That’s bad news for everyone else in the NBA.

It’s already time for a rematch, huh? The Detroit Pistons face the Charlotte Hornets for the second time this season. In the first matchup, the Pistons prevailed 97-89 behind a Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins one-two punch at point guard. Cunningham had 30 points and seven assists, and Jenkins scored 14 points off the bench. They also got great contributions from Paul Reed (16 efficient points) and an all-around masterclass from Ausar Thompson, who tallied seven points, nine rebounds, and eight assists. It featured a great 31-point performance from the blossoming Brandon Miller and one of the season’s earliest head-scratchers. Naz Reid had seven points and six rebounds at halftime, but Hornets coach Charles Lee benched Reid for the entire second half for not meeting the “standards” of the team. Nothing stood out as egregious, and folks chalked it up to mixing up some defensive assignments and a lack of hustle. It was a surprising but short-lived kerfuffle (Reid’s been back in the lineup ever since). But I wouldn’t be surprised if the Hornets power forward is looking to make a statement against Detroit so as to truly put the situation to rest.

The Hornets are struggling to find their offense after moving on from LaMelo Ball and getting a bum hand via injuries — Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams are both going to miss the game tonight. That means the league’s least potent (statistically) offense is going to go up against the league’s most miserly defense (statistically). Detroit’s goal is to make that gulf clear and even wider at the end of the night than it was at the beginning.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Nets final score: Detroit takes care of business in first NBA Cup game
pistons.body:
BROOKLYN, NY - OCTOBER 30: Ronald Holland II #5 of the Detroit Pistons dunks the ball during the game against the Brooklyn Nets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons start the NBA Cup off with a bang. Detroit thumped the Brooklyn Nets 110-94. A plus-16 point differential is a solid start on their quest to win their first NBA Cup in franchise history.

Detroit’s defense got off to an uncharacteristic start. They got mixed up on several pick-and-roll possessions, but that didn’t last long. They figured out the Nets’ speedy guards. Nolan Traoré turns on the turbos when turning the corners. Detroit adjusted to his speed and Julius Randle’s bully ball style of play.

For the second straight game, Detroit held their opponents to a seemingly never-ending scoring drought. The Pistons hard-hedged, blitzed, and switched PnRs depending on their personnel on the floor. It’s a luxury to have so many versatile defenders.

The John Collins at the five lineups always present a different look. It’s a lot of speed out there when Detroit goes small. The lineups with Paul Reed aren’t technically small ball, but J.B. Bickerstaff can employ him so many different ways. Reed is not too much of a drop big, but he pressures guards coming off screens in every other way.

When Detroit did go small, Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter got their hands dirty helping the team gang rebound. It didn’t register in the box score every time, but the fight was there. Huerter was scrappy and hit a pair of first-half triples. His explosion from trey is coming. I will remain patient and will take all the other little things he’s doing.

Robinson is off to a career-best start. The 3s were hit or miss, but he thrived in transition and baited Brooklyn into several turnovers. Robinson is such an educated cutter. Teams press up on him, sticking to him like gum under the desk, but he has no issue using their momentum against them, beelining to the rim.

Robinson and Ausar connected on some backdoor cuts. Their synergy is so evident. They burned another defense with their DHO link-up.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins preview: 3 key stats
lions.body:
Oct 30, 2022; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) sacks Miami Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) during the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-USA TODAY Sports

As the Detroit Lions approach the midway point of their season, it’s been a weird and challenging week to care as deeply about football or celebrate the Vikings win. Most Lions fans, media members, and those within the franchise have been clinging to the progress reports and updates on team captain Jack Campbell, who remains hospitalized with a neck injury suffered in Week 8. The player who was awarded last season’s media Good Guy of the Year award had just welcomed his first child with his wife, Megan, a son named Cooper, in July. And here was the new dad laid up in a hospital bed, still without full movement of his upper body. It was tough to harness that same giddy, football-frenzied feeling for the upcoming game until fans were reminded why this is such a likable team, as Campbell, the player who perfectly embodies this city and this franchise, remained at the forefront of players’ and coaches’ minds throughout the week. They spoke about how they’re playing for 46.

Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said, “Let’s play and prepare like 46. The way you honor him is to wipe those tears from your eyes and make sure you prepare and play like him.”

That’ll get you on board to root for the boys quickly. And suddenly, just like the countless games down the stretch in 2024 that were continually billed as “trap games,” you feel reassured that the Lions won’t let the 1-6 Miami Dolphins sneak up on them. They’ll be looking to fight and take care of business against the team that once called Dan Campbell its head coach and had Sheppard as one of its defensive anchors.

The Dolphins are going through a rebuilding period, but head coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan both come from Green Bay and are all too familiar with the Lions. They have their talent-deficient unit losing but competing, with a number of young players who could become foundational pieces, much like the early Dan Campbell Lions. This week’s preview will examine three key stats and matchups Detroit needs to control to keep its three-game winning streak alive, avoid giving the Dolphins life, and make 46 proud.

Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus.

Good Golly, Miss Ollie

This week’s preview will focus entirely on how the Lions’ defense will coalesce to cover for the absence of Jack Campbell, and how the Dolphins’ offense will understandably try to attack a defense without its green dot. Linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske are expected to handle the primary linebacker snaps, all with expanded roles and added responsibilities. That becomes particularly important given Miami’s recent success pounding the rock with Ollie Gordon since the De’Von Achane injury.

The Dolphins comparisons to the early Dan Campbell-era Lions have been prevalent this week, and one reason for that is Miami’s reliable and developing offensive line. From left to right, Patrick Paul, Kadyn Proctor, Aaron Brewer, Jonah Savaiinaea, and Austin Jackson form an above-average unit with a good mix of proven, reliable veterans and young, ascending players. They’ve started to give the Dolphins a fighting chance by being imposing and winning at the line of scrimmage.

Since Week 4, the Dolphins have shifted their rushing approach, leaning into their offensive line and Gordon’s preferred running schemes by utilizing power concepts on 13.8% of runs (5th) and man/duo concepts on 20.7% of rushing attempts (15th), with considerable success.

With power, which features a backside pulling guard attacking the frontside like a runaway freight train, Miami has averaged 5.7 yards per carry (7th), +0.219 EPA/rush (6th), a 56.3% rushing success rate (5th), and a 25.0% explosive run rate (4th) since Week 4. Power runs will require Detroit’s linebackers to not only process and flow quickly, but also meet the pulling guard in the hole without giving up ground and scrape from the backside. The linebackers need to be firing on all cylinders to match Miami’s physical, downhill approach.

The same goes for defending man/duo concepts, where the Dolphins’ offense has churned out 5.1 yards per carry (5th), +0.122 EPA/rush (5th), a 50.0% rushing success rate (5th), and an 8.3% explosive run rate (15th) since Week 4.

Interestingly, teams haven’t really tested the Lions’ defense with power runs this season, with only 3.1% of rushing attempts (31st) coming on power concepts. Detroit has faced just one such rush since Week 4, which went for minus-4 yards. The Lions have fared well in the small sample size, allowing only 3.4 yards per carry (t-11th) and no explosive plays on their limited snaps defending power. Teams have, however, tested the Lions’ defense up the gut with man/duo concepts, running them on 31.3% of rushing attempts (5th). Detroit has countered that volume by cleaning up those physical runs, allowing just a 33.3% rushing success rate (4th) and 0.6 yards after contact per rush (2nd).

An underrated key to preventing the Dolphins from outmuscling Detroit up the middle with power and man/duo concepts will be whether Tyleik Williams can play with his hair on fire against All-Pro center Aaron Brewer. Brewer understands leverage and angles better than most centers in the league, but he’s also a pivot player who stands just 6-foot-1 and 290 pounds. If the 6-foot-3 Williams, who notably lost a ton of weight this spring to get down to just 325 pounds, can win at the point of attack, overpower Brewer into the backfield, disrupt rushing lanes and timing, and congest the flow of the run play, it’ll go a long way toward making the linebackers’ jobs much easier.

God Forbid a Willis Gets a Little Motion

While the Dolphins’ offense under second-year holdover offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, formerly of the Houston Texans, doesn’t do much well outside of some aspects of its run designs, it does one thing often enough that it might challenge the Detroit Lions’ defense.

The Dolphins’ offense uses pre-snap motion on 74.1% of its snaps, the second-highest rate of any team in the NFL. The league average is only 59.2%, while the Lions’ offense, for comparison’s sake, sits at just 54.5% (24th). What’s interesting is that the Dolphins aren’t particularly better at rushing or passing the football with or without pre-snap motion, remaining bottom 10 in most metrics. The prevalence of the pre-snap motion itself is what’s important here.

The Lions’ defense hasn’t been tested as frequently against pre-snap motion this season, and when it has, there have been some struggles. Detroit has faced pre-snap motion on only 52.1% of its defensive snaps, the second-lowest rate in the NFL.

The Lions have actually excelled at defending the run against pre-snap motion, restricting opponents to -0.16 EPA/rush (4th) and just a 36.7% rushing success rate (4th). Detroit has managed to shut down offenses trying to gain an advantage in the numbers game, manipulate gap assignments, or use motion to stretch the defense geometrically, get defenders out of position, and create rushing lanes. However, issues arise in pass defense against pre-snap motion. Even if the Dolphins haven’t been particularly successful using it, there are still some concerns for Detroit.

Opponents have passed on 63.6% of plays featuring pre-snap motion against the Lions’ defense, the highest pass-to-run ratio in the NFL on such plays. Against pre-snap motion, Detroit’s pass defense has allowed +0.22 EPA/dropback (29th), a 54.1% passing success rate (26th), and an 11.6% explosive pass rate (27th).

The Lions’ coverage unit will need to communicate effectively and trust one another, particularly with a new green dot in either Derrick Barnes or Malcolm Rodriguez and defensive backs adjusting their coverage responsibilities based on the motion. They’ll need to keep an underrated Dolphins receiving group featuring the springy Malik Washington, promising rookies Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, and tight end Greg Dulcich from getting loose and allowing Malik Willis to chunk the ball downfield.

Where There’s a Willis, There’s a Way

Since Week 5, Kelvin Sheppard and the Detroit Lions’ defense have blitzed on only 17.3% of dropbacks, the second-lowest rate in the NFL (the Dolphins, interestingly, are the lowest at 16.1%). In that same span, comparatively, the Vikings have blitzed 75.6% of the time. It’s a noticeable difference for the Lions’ defense over the last month, considering that in Weeks 1-4, Detroit was tied with Miami at a 27.4% blitz rate (t-17th). Sheppard has dialed back the aggression, allowing more defenders to remain in coverage and letting the front four go to work.

That approach remains the best fit for this matchup, as Malik Willis, just like lawyer Walt Worsch with dog bites in Detroiters, is a bit of a mack when it comes to facing extra pass rushers.

Against the blitz, Willis has a 3:0 touchdown-to-interception ratio, a 94.8 passer rating (18th out of 35 qualifying quarterbacks), 6.6 yards per attempt (22nd), and a 46.7% passing success rate (21st). While those numbers aren’t particularly impressive, they’re surprisingly better than his numbers when he doesn’t face a blitz. There’s a reason teams are blitzing the Dolphins on only 30.4% of dropbacks (18th).

As a team, the Dolphins are also averaging 7.1 yards after catch per reception against the blitz, the third-highest mark in the NFL behind only the Bills and Chiefs. Malik Washington is by far Willis’ favorite safety valve when opposing defenses bring extra heat. This season against the blitz, Washington has recorded 16 targets, 14 receptions, 177 receiving yards, one receiving touchdown, and +10.4 receiving EPA (11th). Washington’s 87.5% catch rate on blitz targets ranks tied for fourth among all wide receivers.

Kelvin Sheppard will need to have the patience to let his four-man pass rush get home against Willis. That also means having linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske spend less time firing at the quarterback and more time in coverage. Without their captain directing traffic, how Sheppard balances those coverage responsibilities and keeps Willis from exploiting the blitz will go a long way toward determining whether Detroit can make it four straight wins.

lions.headline: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 injury designations: Lions rule out 5 starters
lions.body:
Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell’s comments throughout the week.

Let’s look at Friday’s practice report and get you up to date on what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

Ruled OUT

C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start

EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion)

LB Jack Campbell (neck)

CB D.J. Reed (hip)

S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 11

Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week.

Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement:

“It was unfortunate we lost Wonnum, but yet, now (Moore) gets more reps. And the reps that he got are valuable, man. There’s no way to duplicate real in time game reps against good opponents and you see growth, you see growth. I saw growth in practice yesterday. So, the more he plays, the better he’s going to get. And we love where he’s going right now.”

Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified.

“Jack continues to improve, which is all great news,” Dan Campbell said on Friday.

Reed said he felt good in the locker room following the game, but he was not cleared to practice this week and will miss this game. Campbell noted that he’s very confident with the team’s depth:

“(Ennis) Rakestraw is getting better. Rock (Ya-Sin) looks healthy and is playing good football. (Roger) McCreary, too. So, I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us. And (Khalil) Dorsey, man, Dorsey’s contributing in a big way. So, I like where we’re at and it’s really a pretty depthwise, it’s a pretty strong room. So yeah, I don’t like the though of not having Reed, but at the same time, I’m encouraged. I’m encouraged. I think we’ll be OK here.”

Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return.

“It’s been great. Two weeks ago, it was classroom work, where we were really locked in. Then it was walkthrough and individual. Yesterday was his first team practice and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like). So it was very encouraging. So now he’s gotta stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him, but he looked awesome yesterday at practice,” O’Neill said on Friday.

Questionable

RB Sione Vaki (ankle) — added to the injury report on Friday

RB Jacob Saylors (neck)

WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib)

Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday’s practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend’s game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability.

Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn’t finish Week 7’s game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back.

St. Brown was injured in Week 7 but told the media on Thursday that, “I’m a little banged up, but I’ll be alright,” and is anticipating playing against the Dolphins.

Not listed with an injury designation

LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe)

CB Rock Ya-Sin (cramps)

S Brian Branch (concussion)

Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth.

Ya-Sin dealt with cramps earlier in the week but still practiced in full each day. He’s potentially in line to challenge for a starting role this week with Reed sidelined.

Branch is nearing the end of the NFL’s concussion protocol, and Campbell said he expects him to be cleared and ready to play on Sunday.

“I think (Brian Branch) BB’s going to be good here. We’ll get through today, and I think we’ll be OK.”

Dolphins’ injury designations

Coming soon.

lions.headline: Lions safety Kerby Joseph looking ‘better than anticipated’
lions.body:
ALLEN PARK, MI - AUGUST 08: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) participates in pass coverage drills during the Detroit Lions Training Camp afternoon practice session on August 8, 2022 at the the Detroit Lions Training Facility in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph won’t play this week, as he continues to ramp up from a knee injury that cost him over a year of football activities. But as he continues to get more work in and get close to his return to the field, Joseph is starting to turn heads.

Last week, the Lions started his 21-day evaluation clock, getting him worked into walkthrough practices while getting additional reps with teammates after practice. This week, he got his first taste of team action, and he was already doing things Lions safeties coach Jim O’Neill wasn’t expecting.

“It’s been great. Two weeks ago, it was classroom work, where we were really locked in. Then it was walkthrough and individual. Yesterday was his first team practice, and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like),” O’Neil said. “So it was very encouraging. So now he’s gotta stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him, but he looked awesome yesterday at practice.”

O’Neil credited a lot of people in Joseph’s recovery. There’s the medical staff that has outlined and executed a recovery plan for the safety. There are players like Dominic Lovett and Jackson Meeks, who have stayed after practice to help get Joseph caught up on the reps he’s missed in practice during his ramp-up. But more than anyone, O’Neil credits Joseph’s perseverance through the difficult last couple of years.

“He’s worked his ass off. He has. He’s gone through a mental battle, he’s gone through a physical battle, and he’s in a great place right now,” O’Neil said. “And I’m excited for him, and I know how hard he’s working. I know how hard it must be to be at the top of your game and then have it taken away from you. He’s grinded to get back to the level that he’s used to playing at and at his standard.”

The next step for Joseph is simple: stack days. It’s not just about how his knee responds to a heavier load, but how Joseph himself can continue to play and grow. As O’Neil is quick to point out, Joseph hasn’t really played at a Pro Bowl level in nearly two years, as he was battling through this knee injury even when he was playing in 2025.

But if the Lions can get the 2024 Kerby Joseph back—along with Brian Branch’s continued progress now that he’s back from his 2025 Achilles injury—then Detroit’s back-end could look a lot different and better soon.

“As we get guys back, guys like with Kerby’s skillset or (Thomas) Harper’s skillset, that just opens up the door to do more stuff with Branch,” O’Neil said. “He can go down, he can do dime roles, he can play nickel roles. You can use him more of a chess piece as we get some guys back in the defense and in that secondary.”

lions.headline: Has the Detroit Lions defense turned a corner?
lions.body:
What a difference a month can make. After a historically bad start to the season, Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has helped the defense find their sea legs over the course of the last four weeks. With that said, there is still plenty to improve upon for a unit that has even more to play for with the loss of All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell during their Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings.

There were some around the fan base and media who were ready to move on from Sheppard if things didn’t improve—especially after the loss to the Carolina Panthers where they appeared to be out-schemed from the jump. After some tough conversations as well as some schematic and personnel tweaks, the Lions’ defense is beginning to settle in dating back to their Week 5 whooping of the Arizona Cardinals.

That brings us to today’s Question of the Day:

Do you believe the Lions’ defense has turned a corner?

My answer: Despite a three-game sample size not being the largest to go off of, I do belive this unit has begun to figure things out. It still isn’t perfect, and there are still too many missed assignments for my liking, but you can do a lot with the way the Lions’ front is playing. Their star players up front, like defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and defensive tackle Alim McNeill, are making their presence felt nearly every time the ball is snapped.

Beyond those two, other members of the defensive line like rookie Skyler Gill-Howard and second year defensive tackle Tyleik Williams are playing some really good football. And while there are still things to clean up in the secondary, cornerback D.J. Reed’s play has really leveled out, star defensive back Brian Branch is back in the mix, and the team opened up All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph’s 21-day window last week.

If they can continue to defend the run well and cut down on the blown coverage moments that have plagued them through seven games, I think that will be enough to make them a contender down the stretch. Continue to improve so that you are playing your best, and most sound football in December and into January. When you have an offense like Detroit does, that’s all you really need.

What about you? Do you think the Lions’ defense has turned a corner? Let us know in the comments below.
